value.title: CLI: import verb + conversation query surface

sections.name: summary
sections.value: The user surface. Key research fact: source_kind is the VECTOR-SPACE axis (raw|smart, CHECK-constrained, job-parsed) -- conversation is NOT a third value on it but an orthogonal content-type filter on elements.kind. The CLI keeps workshop 003s one user-facing --source axis by MAPPING conversation to that filter. Coordinate with w-get-verb (in flight): it builds the conv: dispatch arm returning NOT-IMPLEMENTED; this phase replaces that arm.

value.title: flowspace3 conversation import <file|-> : our JSONL shape (documented); mints/accepts GUID; anchor from cwd git context or flags; RE-IMPORT of a grown file appends only new turns (the iterative contract, proven in a test); claude/omp dialect adapters live in the importer only
value.note: flowspace3 conversation import <file|->, crates/cli/src/conversation.rs. Dialect adapters live in the importer only. The guid is DERIVED from the file name plus its first turn when none is given, which is what makes re-importing a grown file reach the same conversation instead of storing it all again under a new address. Proven on real data in the dogfood run: already_stored 14, accepted 1.

value.title: conversation list + remove verbs (Jordan 2026-08-27): list with anchor filters (--repo, --path prefix) showing guid, title, turn count, started_at, anchor; remove <guid> deletes conversation + turns + element rows and normal gc reclaims the chain -- symmetric with repo remove; both JSON envelopes
value.note: conversation list (--repo, --path prefix) and conversation remove <guid>, both JSON envelopes, GET/POST on /conversations. remove deletes conversation + turns + turn elements by ADDRESS prefix - not by blob, which is shared by construction and would take a twin's identical turn with it - and stops there, leaving shared enrichment to gc.

value.title: search --source conversation: accepts it, maps to a content-type filter -- SearchFilters gains kind (embeddings.rs:292), predicate bound in BOTH the nearest CTE and the element-resolution LATERAL (critic finding 4: resolver picks lowest-id element per raw_hash, so a deduped turn can resolve to a code element without the second predicate); default source=all keeps EXCLUDING turns; conv: arm in address_of (search.rs:274); recency-leaning rank for turns; test: hit on shared turn text resolves to a turn element
value.note: SearchFilters gained kinds (embeddings.rs), bound in BOTH the candidate CTE and the element-resolution LATERAL. MUTATION-CHECKED: remove the predicate from the resolver and a_hit_on_text_shared_with_code_resolves_to_the_turn reports kind function instead of turn - critic finding 4 exactly. A3's anchor leg also landed here: the CTE reaches a repository through turns -> conversations as well as through worktree_files, so --repo narrows conversations instead of erasing them. conv: addresses minted in address_of; default source keeps excluding turns via an exhaustive CODE_KINDS list.

value.title: Windowed fetch + outline: fill the conv: arm (get conv:<guid>#t<ord> --before N --after M) if w-get-verb landed, else flowspace3 conversation show with the same contract; tree conv:<guid> returns the outline
value.note: w-get-verb's conv: arm FILLED rather than a new verb: get returns an untagged GetPayload (element or conversation window) and tree conv:<guid> returns the outline. The guid/turn parse stays in fs3_core::address as ruled; TreeEntry gained role/source/at as skipped-when-absent columns so the outline carries what workshop 005 specifies. Its two NOT-IMPLEMENTED tests were replaced with tests for the implemented behaviour.

value.title: DOGFOOD EXIT PROOF: import a real fleet transcript, grow it with a second import (iterative), semantic-search a known moment, window around the hit; run transcript recorded in the plan folder as exit evidence
value.note: docs/plans/conversations/assets/evidence/dogfood-exit-proof.md, with the transcript beside it. Run against a PRIVATE dogfood database with the REAL Azure embedder and summarizer, so the search is a real embedding and a real LLM summary. Imported this packet's own fleet session, grew it, asked 'why did we drop the foreign key on the anchor' - a question sharing almost no words with the answer - and the top hit was the stop-and-ask itself at 0.606 with its summary competing beside it, the ruling next. Windowed around it and outlined the whole thing. Production verified untouched.
